thesis: Laws constrain models without automatically explaining their ontology or supplying an ultimate foundation.
role: Maps different accounts of order and distinguishes constraints from negotiable conventions.

ideas.statement: Laws, initial conditions, mathematical rules and institutional regularities play distinct roles.
Deeper explanations can reduce assumptions without eliminating them; change may be effective rather than fundamental.
Competing metaphysical accounts have explanatory costs; satisfaction and beauty do not establish truth.
Separate real physical constraints, negotiable institutional rules and unknown model limits.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Noether’s connection between symmetry and conservation has precise assumptions.
Jacobson’s thermodynamic argument changes an equation’s status without revealing a final substrate.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Observer selection needs an explicit distribution; compatible intention does not discriminate empirical results.

audit.notes: Read every unit; fictional examples and limits retained. Structural transitions excluded from ranking.
